title: Physical System Study on Balancing Interactive and Batch Job Performance through Oversubscribing Scheduling
problem: Interactive and batch jobs have conflicting resource requirements in shared HPC systems
motivation: Need practical mechanisms to reduce interactive job queue times without sacrificing system throughput
method: The study tests oversubscribing—running more jobs simultaneously than there are physical processors—on actual server hardware using real workloads instead of simulations. Oversubscribing works because the operating system's scheduler can rapidly switch between jobs, letting quick interactive tasks complete without waiting for long-running batch jobs to finish. By measuring actual memory usage during these experiments, the researchers identified the real constraints on when this strategy is effective.
key_novelty: Oversubscribing proves to be an effective and simpler alternative to complex multi-queue schedulers for balancing interactive and batch jobs.
contributions: Oversubscribing as solution for interactive/batch coexistence
Reduced queue waiting times for interactive jobs
Memory usage insights for capacity planning
